title: Principal-ideal algebraization of a torsion conormal presentation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $a\in A$, and put $P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_{(a)}$ for $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal and let $E=P/J$ be $(a)$-adically complete. Suppose $a^c$ annihilates both the kernel and the cokernel of $\delta:J/J^2\to E^{\oplus r}$, $f\bmod J^2\mapsto(\partial f/\partial x_i\bmod J)_i$, for some $c\geq0$, with continuous derivatives. Then there is a finite type commutative $A$-algebra $C$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat C_{(a)}\cong E$.

proof.text: The polynomial ring $A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is finite type over $A$, so it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Its completion $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and the quotient $E$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. These facts will also apply below to any finite type polynomial quotient over $A$ and its completion.

source.place: Tag 0ALS proof, presentation; Tag 0AJQ, Noetherianity of complete finite-type presentations.

proof.text: Put $M=J/J^2$. Since $a^c\operatorname{coker}\delta=0$, choose $u_i\in M$ with $\delta(u_i)=a^ce_i$ and let $\alpha:E^{\oplus r}\to M$ send $e_i$ to $u_i$. Then $\delta\alpha=a^c\mathrm{id}$. For $m\in M$, $\alpha\delta(m)-a^cm\in\ker\delta$, so $a^c\alpha\delta=a^{2c}\mathrm{id}_M$. Thus $\beta=a^c\alpha$ satisfies both $\delta\beta=a^{2c}\mathrm{id}$ and $\beta\delta=a^{2c}\mathrm{id}$. Choose $f_i\in J$ representing $\beta(e_i)$. Their derivative matrix modulo $J$ is $a^{2c}\mathrm{id}$, so its determinant $\Delta$ in $E$ is $a^{2cr}$. Set $d=2c(r+1)$ and $b=a^{2c}\in E$, so $b\Delta=a^d$; also $a^dJ\subseteq(f_1,\ldots,f_r)+J^2$, because $a^{2c}M$ is in the image of $\beta$. This gives the equations required in the source without introducing a separate Artin-condition lemma.

source.place: Tag 0ALS invoking Tag 0AJU(6); here the two homotopy identities and determinant are written out directly from the kernel/cokernel hypothesis.

proof.text: The subset $U=E[a^\infty]$ is an ideal. It is finitely generated since $E$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Each of its finitely many generators is killed by a power of $a$, so choose $t\geq0$ with $a^tU=0$. If $a^ty\in U$, then some $a^{k+t}y=0$, hence $y\in U$ and $a^ty=0$. Therefore $U\cap a^tE=0$. Put $h=2d$ and choose $n>\max(2h,h+t)$; in particular $n-h\geq1$. For each $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] applied to $A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ supplies a polynomial $f_i^{\prime}$ congruent to $f_i$ modulo $a^nP$. Put $\Delta^{\prime}=\det(\partial f_j^{\prime}/\partial x_i)$ and form the actual finite type algebra $$C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r,z]/(f_1^{\prime},\ldots,f_r^{\prime},z\Delta^{\prime}-a^d).$$ Polynomial differentiation preserves $a^nP$, and a determinant is a polynomial in the entries, so $\Delta^{\prime}\equiv\Delta\pmod {a^nE}$.

source.place: Tag 0GAW polynomial approximation construction, with one generator a and m=r; the bounded-torsion condition for Tag 0AK7 is proved directly using the finite generation of the torsion ideal.

proof.text: Write $Q=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r,z]$, let $L_0$ be its ideal generated by the $r+1$ displayed equations $g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1}$, and put $D=\widehat C_{(a)}$. Both $Q$ and $C$ are Noetherian by Step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] to $0\to L_0\to Q\to C\to0$, and [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] to the finite $Q$-module $L_0$. The image of its completion in $\widehat Q$ is the ideal $L=(g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})\widehat Q$: the tensor formula sends $u\otimes\ell$ to $u\ell$. Consequently $D=\widehat Q/L$. The ring $D$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and is $(a)$-adically complete by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal].

source.place: Tag 0GAW, the completion C^ of the constructed algebra; the completed polynomial presentation is justified by algebra.tex Tags 00MB, 00MA, 0316 and 05GG.

proof.text: Let $V=L/L^2$, let $q:D^{\oplus(r+1)}\twoheadrightarrow V$ send the basis vectors to the classes of the $g_j$, and let $\delta_D:V\to D^{\oplus(r+1)}$ be the continuous derivative map. Its matrix on these generators is $$T=\begin{pmatrix}(\partial f_j^{\prime}/\partial x_i)&(z\partial\Delta^{\prime}/\partial x_i)\\0&\Delta^{\prime}\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det T=(\Delta^{\prime})^2.$$ Here columns index equations and rows index $x_1,\ldots,x_r,z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-adjugate-identity], $H_0=q\operatorname{adj}(T)$ satisfies $\delta_DH_0=(\Delta^{\prime})^2\mathrm{id}$ and $H_0\delta_D=(\Delta^{\prime})^2\mathrm{id}$, the latter first on each generator $q(e_j)$ and then on all of $V$. Since $z\Delta^{\prime}=a^d$ in $D$, the map $H=z^2H_0$ satisfies $\delta_DH=a^{2d}\mathrm{id}$ and $H\delta_D=a^{2d}\mathrm{id}$. In particular $a^h\operatorname{coker}\delta_D=0$, with $h=2d$ independent of the precision $n$.

source.place: Tag 0GAW Jacobian determinant computation and Tag 0GAV (lemma-presentation-rig-smooth); square case, with the adjugate homotopy written out.

proof.text: Define $\psi_n:D\to E/a^nE$ by sending $x_i$ to its original class in $E/a^nE$ and $z$ to the class of $b$. Each $f_i^{\prime}$ maps to zero by its approximation to $f_i\in J$, and $z\Delta^{\prime}-a^d$ maps to $b\Delta-a^d=0$. The map on the completed polynomial ring is defined by reducing to $Q/a^nQ$, using [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], so it factors through $D=\widehat Q/L$. Apply [lem-per-principal-adic-homomorphism-lift] with source $D$, target $E$, nullhomotopy $H$ of Step 5, exponent $h=2d$, and torsion bound $t$ of Step 3. The inequality chosen in Step 3 is exactly its required inequality. It gives an $A$-algebra map $\varphi:D\to E$ congruent to $\psi_n$ modulo $a^{n-h}E$, hence modulo $aE$.

source.place: Tag 0GAW map psi_n and its lift phi; Tag 0ALS final sentence substitutes Tag 0AK7 for general lifting.

proof.text: The classes of the original $x_i$ generate $E/aE$ as an $A/aA$-algebra: by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], $P/aP=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/a$, and $E/aE$ is its quotient. Therefore $\psi_n$ and hence $\varphi$ are surjective modulo $a$. Use [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] with source ring $D$, ideal $aD$, target $E$, and map $\varphi$. Its source is complete by Step 4; its target is Hausdorff since it is complete by hypothesis, in the compatible-sequence sense of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. It follows that $\varphi:D\twoheadrightarrow E$ is surjective. Write $K=\ker\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 0GAW, surjectivity of phi by algebra.tex Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-completed-cotangent-transitivity] to $D\twoheadrightarrow E$ over $(A,(a))$. The ring $D$ is complete by Step 4 and $D/aD=C/aC$ is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] and the construction of $C$; $E$ is complete by hypothesis and its reduction is finite type by Step 7. Choose the presentations $D=\widehat Q/L$ and $E=P/J$. For the relative presentation of $E$ over $D$, use zero variables: $\widehat D_{(a)}=D\twoheadrightarrow E$ has kernel $K$, so its conormal complex is $(K/K^2\to0)$. The cited transitivity sequence therefore contains the exact fragment $$\ker\delta\longrightarrow K/K^2\longrightarrow E\otimes_D\operatorname{coker}\delta_D.$$ The first term is killed by $a^c$ by hypothesis. The third is killed by $a^h$ by Step 5: on a pure tensor $a^h(e\otimes v)=e\otimes a^hv=0$. Thus for $u\in K/K^2$, exactness puts $a^hu$ in the image of $\ker\delta$, and the additional factor $a^c$ kills it. Consequently $a^{h+c}(K/K^2)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GAW final exact-sequence argument using Tag 0ALM; since m=r, the differential cokernel on the source is already power-torsion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-conormal-torsion-algebraization] with Noetherian base $A$, ideal $I=(a)$, finite type algebra $C$ of Step 3, and the surjection $D=\widehat C_{(a)}\twoheadrightarrow E$ of Step 7. Its kernel conormal is annihilated by $a^{h+c}$ by Step 8, equivalently by $I^{h+c}$. The cited statement gives a finite type $A$-algebra $F$ and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat F_{(a)}\cong E$. Renaming $F$ gives the required algebraization.

source.place: Tag 0GAW, final use of more-algebra.tex Tag 0ALR (lemma-quotient-by-idempotent).
